rationale: Thin II Detransitive Preterit, same eye-subject construction as the inherited example but emotional context. English is the supplied project machine translation; the analysis rests on Turoyo.

data.turoyo: Aloh! I naqqa d kmaḥkena, kdəmʕi ʕayni. Tarte damʕe nafəl m ʕayni. <...>
data.translation: God! As we tell it, my eyes shed tears. Two tears fell from my eyes. <...>

rationale: Thin I Infectum, emotional tearing with overt postposed eyes subject. English is the supplied project machine translation; the analysis rests on Turoyo.

summary: Both supplied occurrences are already quoted:11/327 under I Infectum and84/34 within II Detransitive Preterit84/33–34. Thin-cell priority does not justify printing the same passage twice.
Eyes are the overt subject in both passages. Joy in11/327 and sunlight in84/33–34 are stimuli/causes; neither requires a separate lexical sense.
II describes a bodily process without an expressed agent, while I also describes spontaneous tearing. The two attestations do not establish a systematic semantic opposition between the stems.
Both Jan tokens retain eyes as grammatical subject, not the whole human experiencer. I kdəmʕi and II Detransitive mdamʕi have the same bodily process in emotional contexts.

Emotional versus physical cause does not establish a new sense, and Jan does not resolve the round-1 question about an aspectual or dialectal I/II contrast. The inherited II Detransitive Preterit filing is retained for the exact parallel form.
Is there a stable dialectal or aspectual difference between I and II? One example per contextual type cannot establish it.
Compare11/327 source gdəmʕi with glossary gəd-dumʕi against the edition before any fix-text; preserve both supplied witnesses.
Does mdamʕi in Jan 1.8/201 denote onset or an ongoing/resulting state? The machine English full of tears does not decide the paradigm.
Emotional grief/family discussion also triggers eye tearing; the inherited sunlight stimulus is not a lexical restriction.
